newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee ends down vs dlr, forward premia eases.
newsitem.headline: India rupee ends down vs dlr, forward premia eases.

text.p: The Indian rupee weakened on heavy dollar demand to end Monday at 35.92/94 against the opening quotes of 35.85/86, dealers said.
They said heavy dollar buying by a large state-run bank from eastern India pushed the rupee down in active trade.
The rupee traded at a high of 35.845 and stray deals were done as low as 35.96, they said.
"Good business was done at 35.93 and 35.94," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "Only stray deals at 35.96 ... once it was clear the state-run bank was not buying at these levels, the rupee rallied."
Dealers said the state-run bank bought dollars at various levels from 35.87 rupees to 35.935.
Premia on forward dollars eased on prospects of improved domestic liquidity, dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India said last week banks' cash reserve ratio (CRR) requirements would be cut by 50 basis points to 10.5 percent on January 4.
The premia on six-month dollars ended Monday at an annualised 7.18 percent against the weekend close of 7.42 percent, dealers said.
"With a cut in cash reserves coming in next week, the sentiment is definitely weak," said a dealer. "Receiving pressure is fairly strong."
